title: Simultaneous Fourier failure probability
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$ with $1<n$, and let $p\in[0,1]$. Choose a random function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ by assigning independent values, each equal to $1$ with probability $p$ and $0$ otherwise. Put $\tau_n=2\sqrt n\,2^{-n/2}$. The probability that either the constant Fourier coefficient differs from $p$ by more than $\tau_n$, or some nonempty Fourier index has coefficient of absolute value greater than $\tau_n$, is at most $2^{-n}$.
